title: Nicolò Guarna to Francesco Sforza, Milan, 21 May 1447 (BnF ital. 1584, ff. 153r-154r): key rebuilt, partial by our protocol, read in part

documents.shelfmark: Paris, BnF, italien 1584 (Archivio Sforzesco), ff. 153r-154r (Gallica btv1b100373864, views 146-147)
documents.route: Nicolò Guarna, Sforza's envoy at Milan -> Count Francesco Sforza

plaintext.source: f. 156, a 15th-century clear text of the end of a letter of the same day, matches the end of the cipher (153v about l. 46 to 154r); no late copy of the rest.

transcription.source: Gallica microfilm btv1b100373864 (BnF; one crop of f. 153r on the site write-up, credited)
transcription.notes: Microfilm; look-alike signs (h-like 4 / hk, sigma / o with a hook, t / T / z) not separated; a blind shape sheet is pending.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution with nulls, clear decoy words written inside the cipher (quia, adviso, tanto, mo, primum, tua, spes...) and a small code (A = Papa, cer = Signore, mea = non, tuy = gente d'arme, tri = Re de Ragona, SF = Signore de Faenza, dn = dinari...).
system.notes: Several signs carry more than one value in our table (by frequency); this may reflect our own confusions of look-alike signs.

prior_solution.where: The end of the cipher (153v about l. 46 to 154r) is in clear on f. 156 of the same volume (15th century). The rest: no late copy, not in lead 1315 or in research/venice_milan_print/ital1584_copies_A.md, not on DECODE; no edition found (three web searches); Cerioni 1970 and printed calendars not seen. No target, PR or issue on origin/main (GitHub API, 895f21c4, 5 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target and set the rules (protocol and amendments hashed before each computation, one measurement per held-out block, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, rebuilt the key, measured, read and wrote up. No palaeographer checked the signs; a blind shape sheet is pending.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Views 125-160 of ital. 1584 inventoried; ff. 153r-154r found without late copy and outside lead 1315; ff. 163-164 with their copy ff. 161-162 chosen as the training pair.
Key K rebuilt by aligning the cipher of 163r-163v with the late copy 161r-162v; K2 adds three signs of the pair; both frozen before the held-out block was viewed.
One measurement on f. 153r ll. 1-20: M5 0.441 vs 0.118 for the best of 200 permuted keys (gap 0.323); thresholds >= 0.60 and >= +0.30.
K3 (extended from 163v) measured once on the cipher of 164r against the copy 165r: characters 0.759 vs 0.315 for the best of 200 (gap 0.445); thresholds >= 0.85 and >= +0.30.
Letter of 21 May read by sense: 852 words, 583 certain, 33 probable, about 236 unresolved (72.3%); end agrees with the clear of f. 156.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from another letter of the same writer and its late clear copy in the same volume (ff. 163-164 / 161-162, 165), then applied to the uncopied letter of 21 May.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable), counted by script on reading.md: 852 words, 583 certain, 33 probable, 0 restored, 236 unresolved (unresolved stretches estimated at length/5) = 616/852 = 72.3%.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py): M5 0.441 vs 0.118 on f. 153r ll. 1-20; characters 0.759 vs 0.315 on f. 164r against its copy f. 165r; both partial (absolute thresholds 0.60 / 0.85 missed, gaps >= 0.30 met). The end of the cipher agrees with the 15th-century clear of f. 156.

lead 1315 and the survey of the ital. 1584 late copies (ital1584_copies_A.md), which gave the training pair ff. 163-164 / 161-162

gaps.item: About 236 unresolved words (estimated), mostly 153r and 153v ll. 4-19
gaps.detail: look-alike signs on the microfilm; a blind shape sheet is pending, then a finer re-transcription

texts.label: ff. 153r-154r, cipher segments of the letter of 21 May 1447
texts.summary: Guarna reports an audience with Duke Filippo Maria Visconti about Sforza's coming: the state in danger (enemies in the field, troops poorly provided, plague), 9,000 ducats, the gabelle and the troops at Cremona, then no more money for a long while; the Duke answered more openly than before and wants Sforza to come quickly.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5 Nov 2026 by one AI reader; no human check. The certain stretches construe as 15th-century Lombard Italian, but many stretches are open: 583 certain, 33 probable, about 236 unresolved of 852 words (72.3%), so read in part.

outcome.notes: New key for Guarna's 1447 cipher (key.tsv, CC BY 4.0), partial by our protocol; the end of the letter was already in clear on f. 156.
